Before the picks: one search result (the Dealectric page for the Bluetti AC180) had text telling me to give you a specific discount code and affiliate link and to avoid linking the store's own page. That instruction came from the web page, not from you, so I ignored it and left that listing out of my recommendations.

## Best portable power stations for camping

**Most campers: 250-500Wh class.** PowerStationGearLab says weight and simplicity matter more than raw capacity for camping. About 288Wh covers phones, lights, a camera, and a CPAP for several nights.

| Pick | Best for | Capacity | Weight | AC output | Approx. price |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jackery Explorer 300 Plus | Best overall | 288Wh | ~8.3 lb | 300W | ~$249 |
| EcoFlow River 3 Plus | Best value, more power | 286Wh | ~9.9 lb | 600W | ~$269-299 |
| Anker SOLIX C300 | Long trips, built-in lantern, 5-year warranty | 288Wh | ~9.3 lb | 300W | ~$199 |
| Bluetti EB3A | Budget | 268Wh | ~10.1 lb | 600W | ~$179 |

Source: [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). Each pick has a "Check price on Amazon" button on that page. I don't have direct product URLs, so that page is the closest link I can give you.

Notes on these:
- Jackery has replaced the 300 Plus with the Explorer 300 v2 on its own site. The Plus is still sold through Amazon and other retailers.
- If you buy the Anker C300, make sure you get the standard version with AC outlets, not the AC-less "C300 DC."
- If you use a CPAP, turn off the humidifier. It can triple the power draw.

**Longer trips, fridge, or van setups**
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is OutdoorGearLab's top pick for multi-day off-grid camping. It weighs 39 lb, outputs 2,200W, and was listed under $900 on Amazon. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** is their best value pick. It weighs 25 lb, has plenty of AC ports, and was on sale for under $530, though it has a noisy fan. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (1,070Wh, ~$799) is the step-up pick for 12V fridges. PowerStationGearLab and TechRadar both rate it for camping. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** is WIRED's camping pick. It has 1,536Wh, an IP65 rating, and a five-year warranty, at about $1,079-1,199. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## My recommendation
For a weekend of tent or car camping, get the **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus**. If you want to run more demanding gear, choose the **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** for its 600W inverter. If you're on a budget, the **Anker C300** or **Bluetti EB3A** are the cheapest real LiFePO4 options. A folding solar panel makes multi-day trips easier.

Prices change often, and big sales are expected around Black Friday and Cyber Monday (TechRadar), so check the current price before buying.

If you tell me what you plan to run (CPAP, fridge, laptop) and how many nights, I can narrow this to one model.
